complexity_matrix.operation: Single bitwise operation (AND, OR, XOR, NOT, shift)
complexity_matrix.notes: One instruction on a fixed-width word, independent of how many bits are set.
Must use 1u or 1ULL; shifting into the sign bit of a signed type is undefined behaviour.
Subtracting one flips the low set bit and sets all lower bits; the AND keeps only the bits above it.
Relies on two's complement, which C++20 guarantees. Use std::countr_zero for the portable form.
Runs once per set bit. Hardware POPCNT reduces this to a single instruction on a word.
Constant time, but only for one word: the word-level bound does not extend to unbounded widths.

complexity_matrix.operation: XOR of a whole array to find the odd element out
complexity_matrix.notes: Correct only when every value appears an even number of times except one; otherwise it returns a plausible but meaningless value.

complexity_matrix.operation: Range XOR query via prefix array
complexity_matrix.notes: After O(n) preprocessing. A genuine asymptotic improvement over rescanning the range.

complexity_matrix.operation: Submask enumeration of a k-bit mask
complexity_matrix.notes: s = (s-1) & m visits every non-empty submask exactly once. Exponential, with no wasted iteration.

complexity_matrix.operation: Bitset union / intersection / difference over W elements
complexity_matrix.notes: A 64-fold constant-factor gain over a boolean array. Both forms are still Theta(W).
Works even when both operands are the same variable, unlike the temporary-swap idiom.
Needs compare-and-swap or fetch_or; the plain compound assignment is a read-modify-write and loses updates under contention.

correctness_argument.claim: XOR cancels pairs because it is associative and commutative so elements may be regrouped, and x XOR x is zero, so even-multiplicity groups vanish while odd-multiplicity groups collapse to a single copy. Each mask operation affects exactly one bit position because OR with zero, AND with one and XOR with one are all identity or constant on every other position.

cost_derivations.claim: Every bitwise operation is O(1) on a fixed-width word, so the number of operations never changes and only constants move, by at most the word size. Bitsets gain a factor of 64 per operation over boolean arrays while remaining Theta(W), and a range-XOR prefix array converts an O(range) scan into an O(1) query after O(n) preprocessing.
cost_derivations.detail: Kernighan popcount is O(set bits) because each step clears exactly one; hardware POPCNT is O(1) per word but does not extend to unbounded widths.

limits.claim: No bitwise trick improves asymptotic complexity, since every operation is O(1) and only the constant moves. Fixed-width arithmetic cannot represent unbounded values, so beyond the word width each operation costs O(limbs) and the advantage disappears. Concurrent bit manipulation needs atomics because compound assignment is a read-modify-write. Signed shifts and 1 << 31 are undefined behaviour, not merely implementation-defined, which is why every bit routine should take unsigned parameters.

supporting_structure.name: Bit-Mask Set
supporting_structure.rationale: Bitwise techniques do not operate on collections; they operate on a single word of packed flags. Every mask idiom the topic teaches -- set a flag, test a flag, clear a flag, check a subset -- is a shift and a mask against that word, so the bit set is not a container introduced to satisfy the exercise rule but the operand the technique is defined over.
